GENE.definition_en: Mentions of genes or gene products in biomedical text. Include symbols, names, and common variants used by authors; annotate by exact character offsets. Exclude diseases, chemicals, species/organisms, cell types, pathways, and experimental procedures.

final_task_goal: This task constructs a single-label gene mention corpus optimized for robust mention detection and normalization-ready outputs. * Document pool and source: English biomedical literature with sentences drawn primarily from MEDLINE/PubMed abstracts; sentences are annotated at character offsets to reflect real-world author usage. * Purpose of NER: Identify contiguous spans corresponding to gene or gene product mentions and record start–end character offsets. Support alternate acceptable boundaries to mitigate ambiguity during evaluation. * Entity types: One category—GENE—covering genes and gene products only. Non-gene biomedical entities such as chemicals, diseases, species, and cell types are out of scope. * Downstream applications: Enable gene normalization to database identifiers and cross-resource linking; serve as upstream signals for relation extraction tasks such as protein–protein interaction extraction; compatible with instruction-tuned NER pipelines for multi-corpus training and evaluation.
